items.title: Abhijeet Dipke detained by Delhi Police ahead of the 5 PM 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Connaught Place
items.summary: Delhi Police detained CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke at ~5:00 PM IST on Friday, minutes ahead of the scheduled 5 PM 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Central Park, Connaught Place (ANI video carried on The Daily Jagran live blog). Police told him "We are placing you under preventive detention," citing Section 163 BNSS prohibitory orders in CP and no NDMC permission for the march (inshorts, published 11:29:15Z). A crowd had already started gathering around Central Park ~4:48 PM despite the closure. This is Dipke's second detention in a week (first: Oct 10, off the Mumbai-Delhi flight). Confirmed internationally by Reuters and CNN; @indianexpress (11:40:20Z) and @timesofindia (11:24:45Z) posted detention footage/graphic on IG. Note (single-source, nationpress FAQ): party legal head Ratna Singh says release-proceedings paperwork for Das/Ranka was completed but delayed by officials, and CJP will challenge the detentions in court.
items.source_name: ANI via The Daily Jagran (live blog); Reuters; CNN; inshorts

items.title: Dipke's video message to PM Modi after police notice: 'Why are you against Tiranga?'
items.summary: Follow-up to the earlier-alerted march-buildup item: the contents of Dipke's ~4:27 PM video message are now public — "Heavy police force deployed at the gate just to stop Tiranga. Why are you against Tiranga, @narendramodi?" (Dipke's own X post via The Daily Jagran live blog). The message was recorded after Delhi Police served him the Section 163 notice at NCP-SCP spokesperson Anish Gawande's residence, asking him not to hold the march; inshorts/latestly carry video of him signing the notice. Gawande backed the march, saying participants planned to unfurl the flag and return peacefully (India Today).
items.source_name: Abhijeet Dipke (X post) via The Daily Jagran (live blog); latestly; inshorts

items.title: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh accuses Congress/INDIA bloc of seeking Bangladesh-style 'regime change' via youth protests
items.summary: At a Lucknow press conference, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh accused Congress and its allies of using the EC/SIR protests to seek a Bangladesh-style 'regime change' and turning youth into 'pawns in the politics of chaos/anarchy' — a 'conspiracy to seize power by inciting anarchy in the country' (PTI via news89). He directly attacked Rahul Gandhi, dismissing his duplicate/fake-voter claims as baseless and noting Congress has filed no formal appeals or evidence; he told Gandhi to respect the mandate and self-introspect (Mirror Now). UP BJP chief Pankaj Chaudhary echoed the 'conspiracy to destabilise' line in Lucknow (ANI via devdiscourse). TBS reports Singh's remarks were a response to Prashant Bhushan's statement at a Press Club of India presser yesterday (alongside Dipke and Neha Bora) that they seek regime change 'and there is nothing wrong with it' (single-source). Also in the live blog: WB BJP's Dilip Ghosh accused CJP of disrupting Durga Puja celebrations.
items.source_name: PTI via news89; Mirror Now; TBS; ANI via devdiscourse

items.title: CATCH-UP: DMK MP Kanimozhi joins student organisations' protest in Chennai demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's removal, SIR withdrawal
items.summary: CATCH-UP (never alerted): DMK MP Kanimozhi joined a student organisations' protest in Chennai demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's removal and withdrawal of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls (PTI video via The Daily Jagran live blog, ~12:34 PM IST). Earlier the same day, student organisations and civil society members held an anti-CEC/SIR protest in Chennai (PTI). Kanimozhi accused the Centre of lacking faith in the Constitution, alleged ~1 lakh voters removed in Kolathur against ~20,000 warranted, claimed Maharashtra roll changes benefited BJP, and said the DMK stands with protesting youth (Asianet Newsable/khelja.in, ANI-syndicated). The protest used Periyar-like models as symbolic elements, with VCK's Thol. Thirumavalavan also present (news89 citing India Today).
items.source_name: PTI via The Daily Jagran (live blog); Asianet Newsable (khelja.in); news89 (citing India Today)

items.title: CATCH-UP: CP traders write to PM Modi (and CJI, LoP) over protest losses; claim Rs 250 crore/day hit, 70% footfall drop
items.summary: CATCH-UP (never alerted): trade bodies wrote to PM Modi, the CJI and LoP Rahul Gandhi over protest-related business losses, seeking immediate intervention (ANI via The Daily Jagran live blog, ~4:16 PM IST; Jagran article published 10:25 AM IST). CP traders claim Rs 250 crore/day business loss and up to 70% footfall drop (2-3 lakh daily visitors down to 40,000-50,000) since the Oct-2 protests; New Delhi Traders Association president Atul Bhargava told ANI business fell to 10% during the CJP protest (devdiscourse), and DL Madan (Janpath) said some shops had no first sale for five Navratri days. A restaurant owner separately approached the Delhi HC seeking compensation for protest losses (devdiscourse). The Supreme Court (CJI Surya Kant + Justice Joymalya Bagchi) listed the Kirana Committee/Iron Traders Association writ against the CJP and Congress protests for Oct 26, warning it could intervene — 'We will act' — if restrictions unlawfully hurt business (livemint).
items.source_name: ANI via The Daily Jagran; livemint; devdiscourse
